label: Model Foundations & Behavior
description: How foundation models are built and how they behave: architectures, training dynamics, tokenization, sampling, scaling, and capability or alignment properties of the model itself.
include: Talks whose primary object is the model: architecture, pretraining, scaling laws, tokenization, sampling, or intrinsic behavior
Capability, hallucination, or alignment findings about the model rather than a product wrapping it
exclude: Serving, batching, or inference-engine talks belong in inference_model_systems
SFT, RLHF, DPO, or continual-learning talks belong in post_training_continual_learning

label: Inference & Model Systems
description: Serving trained models in production: batching, KV cache, quantization, speculative decoding, inference engines, and latency/cost tradeoffs.
include: Primary focus is serving, inference performance, or model-system runtime
Quantization, speculative decoding, or KV-cache engineering as the main subject
exclude: Training or post-training methods are not the primary subject
Application UX around a hosted model belongs in ai_product_ux_human_factors

label: AI Data Engineering
description: Data work that makes models and agents useful: pipelines, labeling, synthetic data, curation, quality, and evaluation datasets as data products.
include: Primary focus is data collection, labeling, synthetic generation, curation, or data quality for AI systems
Dataset construction as an engineering discipline rather than a one-off benchmark mention
exclude: Retrieval indexes and RAG pipelines belong in retrieval_search_knowledge
Post-training recipes that merely consume data belong in post_training_continual_learning

label: Post-Training & Continual Learning
description: Adapting models after pretraining: SFT, RLHF, DPO, continued pretraining, LoRA, unlearning, and enterprise continual-learning systems.
include: Primary focus is fine-tuning, preference optimization, continued pretraining, or continual learning
Parameter-efficient adaptation or unlearning as the main subject
exclude: Prompt-only adaptation belongs in prompting_llm_programming
Serving fine-tuned models belongs in inference_model_systems

label: Prompting & LLM Programming
description: Programming models with language: prompt design, structured output, few-shot patterns, and compiler-like LLM programming systems.
include: Primary focus is prompts, structured generation, or LLM-as-program patterns
DSPy-like or compiler-style prompt optimization as the main subject
exclude: Long-context, memory, or state management belongs in context_engineering_memory
Tool calling and protocol design belong in tools_protocols_integrations

label: Context Engineering & Memory
description: What enters the model context and how state persists: window management, memory systems, compaction, scratchpads, and long-running state.
include: Primary focus is context construction, memory, compaction, or durable conversational state
Engineering the working set the model sees across turns
exclude: Document retrieval and indexes belong in retrieval_search_knowledge
Agent loop or planner design belongs in agent_architecture_harnesses

label: Retrieval, Search & Knowledge
description: Finding and grounding knowledge: RAG, embeddings, hybrid search, knowledge bases, and ranking for generation.
include: Primary focus is retrieval, search, embeddings, or knowledge-base design for AI systems
RAG architecture, chunking, or ranking as the main subject
exclude: Generic data pipelines without retrieval belong in ai_data_engineering
Memory that is not retrieval-backed belongs in context_engineering_memory

label: Agent Architecture & Harnesses
description: How agents are structured: loops, planning, multi-agent patterns, harnesses, and the control plane around a model.
include: Primary focus is agent loops, planning, multi-agent design, or harness architecture
The talk is about the agent system, not a single tool or a single workflow engine
exclude: Durable workflow engines and queues belong in orchestration_durable_execution
SWE-agent product talks whose core is coding belong in coding_agents_software_engineering

label: Tools, Protocols & Integrations
description: How models call the world: tool calling, MCP, A2A, function calling, connectors, and integration protocols.
include: Primary focus is tool calling, protocol design, or integrating external systems
MCP, A2A, or function-calling contracts as the main subject
exclude: The agent loop that uses tools belongs in agent_architecture_harnesses
Durable execution of those calls belongs in orchestration_durable_execution

label: Orchestration & Durable Execution
description: Making agent and model work survive failure: workflows, queues, retries, checkpoints, and durable execution runtimes.
include: Primary focus is workflows, queues, retries, or durable execution for AI work
Crash-safe long-running agent or pipeline orchestration
exclude: In-memory agent loops without durability belong in agent_architecture_harnesses
Observability of those runs belongs in observability_reliability_llmops

label: Coding Agents & Software Engineering
description: Agents that write, review, and ship software: IDE agents, PR agents, codegen, and SWE-bench-style engineering systems.
include: Primary focus is coding agents, software-engineering agents, or AI-in-the-IDE/PR loop
Code generation, repair, or review as the main product or research object
exclude: General agent architecture without a coding focus belongs in agent_architecture_harnesses
Evaluation methodology without a coding-agent system belongs in evaluation_testing_benchmarking

label: Evaluation, Testing & Benchmarking
description: Measuring AI systems: evals, benchmarks, judges, test suites, and measurement methodology.
include: Primary focus is evaluation design, benchmarks, judges, or testing methodology
How quality is measured rather than how a single system is built
exclude: Production tracing and quality monitoring belong in observability_reliability_llmops
A system talk that merely reports one score is not primarily this category

label: Observability, Reliability & LLMOps
description: Operating AI systems: tracing, logging, quality monitoring, incident response, and LLMOps.
include: Primary focus is production observability, reliability, or operating LLM systems
Tracing, quality monitors, or incident response for model/agent products
exclude: Offline eval design belongs in evaluation_testing_benchmarking
Security incidents and guardrails belong in security_safety_identity_governance

label: Security, Safety, Identity & Governance
description: Keeping AI systems safe and governable: prompt injection, authz, identity, guardrails, policy, and compliance.
include: Primary focus is security, safety, identity, authorization, or governance of AI systems
Prompt injection, jailbreaks, or policy controls as the main subject
exclude: Model-intrinsic alignment research belongs in model_foundations_behavior
Generic reliability without a security/governance frame belongs in observability_reliability_llmops

label: Multimodal & Realtime Systems
description: Voice, vision, video, speech, and realtime interactive systems beyond text-only agents.
include: Primary focus is multimodal models or realtime voice/vision/video systems
Speech, streaming interaction, or embodied-adjacent realtime loops
exclude: Text-only agent architecture belongs in agent_architecture_harnesses
Product UX around a multimodal feature without systems depth belongs in ai_product_ux_human_factors

label: AI Product, UX & Human Factors
description: How people use AI products: UX, human-in-the-loop, trust, collaboration, and product design.
include: Primary focus is product design, UX, human-in-the-loop, or trust in AI products
How humans supervise, correct, or collaborate with the system
exclude: Platform/SDK talks for builders belong in ai_platforms_developer_tooling
Security/trust as governance rather than UX belongs in security_safety_identity_governance

label: AI Platforms & Developer Tooling
description: Infrastructure for builders: gateways, playgrounds, SDKs, eval platforms, and developer platforms that other teams build on.
include: Primary focus is a platform, SDK, gateway, or developer tool for building AI systems
The talk is about the substrate other engineers use, not one end-user application
exclude: A single coding agent product belongs in coding_agents_software_engineering
A single workflow engine without a platform frame belongs in orchestration_durable_execution
